verdict: Coin movement is sound on the normal command, job and settlement paths I traced, and determinism is well built, but the load path can conjure coins, the published money total that drives prices is not the coin supply, defense purchases destroy goods twice over, and facilities held by the bank can go bankrupt mid-auction. Nothing here was executed: every finding comes from reading the code, so magnitudes are reasoned, not measured.

read_in_full: Assets/_Game/Agents/ (all 51 files except as listed under skimmed: every system, job, command and table, including MoneyLedger, MoneyTotals, BankSystem, Credit, MerchantJob, MerchantJobTrips, MerchantFlowJob, ProductionSystem, ProductionJobs, PolicySystem)
skimmed: Assets/_Game/Data/SimulationConfig.cs (searched for the money, loan, auction and policy defaults only)
Assets/_Game/Tests/EditMode/ (searched for conservation, save and defense tests; read FinanceTests.cs lines 70-99)
Docs/GDD/03_Decisions.md and Docs/GDD/systems/ (searched for the decisions each finding touches)
Assets/StreamingAssets/Data/ (config.csv and facilities.csv read in full, recipes.csv first 60 lines)
not_read: Assets/StreamingAssets/Data/ map, goods, events, profiles and specialties files
Docs/GDD/reviews/ (not read, as instructed; only its folder names were listed)

findings.title: State defense purchases remove goods twice: from stock at once and again through demand at repricing
findings.evidence: DefensePurchaseJob.Buy does `Stock[c] -= (int)units; Demand[c] = ...Demand[c] + units` and has no Supply field. Every other purchase (MarketFlows.Buy, ProductionJob.UseInput, BuyLoad, MerchantFlowJob.Move, OrderSystem.Collect) also adds the units to Supply, so they pass through. PriceKernel.Step then computes `available = s + st; traded = min(d, available)`, so the demand consumes units a second time. The only test (StateProjectTests.cs:23) checks money spent, not stock.
findings.failure_scenario: A cell has stock 100, no supply and no other demand. Defense buys 10 and pays for 10: stock 90, demand 10. At repricing available is 90, traded is 10, remaining stock is 80. Twenty units left the market for ten paid. DeliveredValue also counts the phantom demand, so households in that market receive and pay for 10 fewer units, and the price sees pressure from demand with no matching supply. This runs every 4 weeks in every nation (defense.interval default 4, share 5% of the yearly budget).
findings.fix: Add Supply to DefensePurchaseJob and do `Supply[c] += units` beside the Demand add, as MarketFlows.Buy does. This changes golden hashes.

findings.title: Loading replaces any facility cash of exactly -1 with its starting cash, conjuring coins
findings.evidence: `if (_facilities.Cash[f] == FacilityTableV1Migration.UnsetCash) _facilities.Cash[f] = StartCash(f);` runs on every load, for current saves too. UnsetCash is -1, which is also a legal arrears value: FacilityUpkeepJob lets cash go below zero by any amount.
findings.failure_scenario: A facility ends a turn with cash -1 and the game is saved and loaded. Its cash becomes 500, 2,000 or 1,000 by tier, so ContinentMoney exceeds CoinSupply by that amount plus one, permanently and silently. The loaded game's hash and future also differ from the same game without the load, and its NegativeCashWeeks run stops. How often a cash of exactly -1 occurs was not measured; with many facilities in arrears it is a matter of time.
findings.fix: Make the sentinel unreachable: have the V1 migration write long.MinValue, or write a separate marker that only the migration path resolves. Fund the migrated start cash from households so old saves stay conserved too.

findings.title: A facility held by the bank for auction can go bankrupt, return to Owner=Npc with the auction still open, and be funded from the wrong group
findings.evidence: FacilityUpkeepJob adds to Bankrupt with no owner check. GoBankrupt only asks wasPlayer and whether an NPC loan exists, then sets `Owner[f] = OwnerIds.Npc`. SeizeFacilities sets Owner=Bank but, unlike NpcLending.SeizeFacility, neither clears arrears nor resets NegativeCashWeeks. It also leaves Group as the player's company, and GoBankrupt only replaces Group when wasPlayer.
findings.failure_scenario: A broke player's facility has cash below zero and NegativeCashWeeks 4 when the bank seizes it at turn T (defaults: bankrupt at 5 weeks, auction 2 weeks). At T+1 upkeep makes it 5 and GoBankrupt runs. (a) The auction row survives but Owner is Npc, so at T+2 BuyFacilityCommand passes; the player pays value plus cash, then Close in the same turn finds no bid and sells it to a family, so the player loses both price and facility. (b) FundNewOperator takes the start cash from the player's company. If the company's headquarters is on another continent, coins leave that continent's money and appear on this one, breaking ContinentMoney == CoinSupply on both. (c) The new operator is funded again at Close.
findings.fix: Skip OwnerIds.Bank in the job's bankruptcy check, and have SeizeFacilities settle arrears and reset NegativeCashWeeks as NpcLending.SeizeFacility does.

findings.title: The published money total driving the price index omits noble purses and all negative balances, so it is not the coin supply
findings.evidence: ContinentMoney adds `households.Cash[node] + households.Spent[node] + houses.Cash[node]`; MoneyTotals.Recompute has no NobleState at all. It also skips non-positive cash (`if (amount <= 0) return`, `if (purses.Float[p] <= 0) continue`). FinanceSystem then does `_currency.MoneyTotal[c] = record.ContinentTotal[c]`, and UpdateRates sets `PriceIndex = FromRatio(MoneyTotal, BaselineMoneyTotal)`. CurrencyState's doc says the total is every coin held, counted once, kept equal to the coin supply.
findings.failure_scenario: At the record of week 51, houses hold what is left of last year's tax share (spending 2% a week), and facilities and merchants in arrears hold negative cash. The total reads low by the noble purses and high by the arrears, because the coins those holders overspent sit elsewhere and are counted. With conserved coins and no minting the price index and exchange rates still move, by an amount set by arrears and tax timing rather than by money. Size not measured.
findings.fix: Publish ContinentMoney for the continent total, or add noble cash and stop discarding negatives. Keep the nation cash display separate if arrears should not show there.

findings.title: Buying goods from a deposit bypasses the bank-run withdrawal limit
findings.evidence: BankTransferCommand caps a run withdrawal at BankRunWithdrawShare of the deposit, once a week. BuyGoodsCommand.Funds returns `funds + Math.Min(bank.PlayerDeposit[nation], bank.Reserve[nation])` with no FinanceState check, and Apply takes the shortfall from deposit and reserve.
findings.failure_scenario: During a bank run a player holds a 100,000 deposit, so the rule allows 10,000 this week. Standing at a branch market, they issue BuyGoodsCommand(..., payFromDeposit: true) repeatedly. Each order is limited only by stock, cart room and funds, and a warehouse or guild hall at the same node frees the cart for the next order, so more than the cap can leave the failing bank in one week, into goods they can resell. DEC-044 and SYS_BANKING line 198 limit the player's withdrawal.
findings.fix: In Funds, during a BankRun, limit the deposit part to the withdrawal cap and record LastWithdrawTurn in Apply, or refuse payFromDeposit during a run.

findings.title: The player's insurance refunds cash losses but is priced only on cargo, so it covers carried coins for free
findings.evidence: Premium: `config.InsurancePremium.MulInt(valueHere)`, the cargo's value. Refund: `Insurance ? config.InsuranceRefund.MulInt(value) : 0`, where value is 30% of the departure coins on a cash loss. The merchant job says the opposite: 'The policy covers no coins'.
findings.failure_scenario: A player with an empty cart and 1,000,000 coins sends TravelCommand(dest, insurance: true). The premium is 0. A cash encounter takes 300,000 and refunds 240,000, paid by the guild and then by the origin's households, so insurance cost nothing and cut the loss by 80%. SYS_ROUTE_HAZARDS records the refund as [Draft], but nothing prices it; no NPC has this.
findings.fix: Refund cargo losses only, as for merchants, or price the premium on cash carried as well.

findings.title: The ship's larger capacity cannot be used: every way of loading goods is limited to the cart
findings.evidence: All player cargo lives in CargoHolders.PlayerCart. BuyGoodsCommand.Fill uses PlayerTrade.CartCapacity, and MoveCargoCommand and MoveGuildHallCargoCommand use CartMaxWeight/CartMaxSize. PlayerTrip.Carrier is the only reader of ShipMaxWeight and only checks a load when departing. Tests exceed the cart by calling CargoTable.Change directly.
findings.failure_scenario: A player buys a ship for 5,000 and docks at a port with 400 weight loaded (the sample cart limit). A further buy fills 0 and is rejected, and a warehouse or hall move finds no room, so the load can never pass 400 although the ship allows 3,000. DEC-034, marked [Confirmed] in SYS_INVENTORY, says an owned ship carries more, and the purchase buys nothing beyond the passage fee.
findings.fix: Use the ship's capacity when it is docked at the player's node in the three Fill methods, and decide what happens to an overfull cart at departure on land (CargoFits already refuses it).

findings.title: Long-lived GroupDirectory instances keep a stale lookup across a load when the group count matches
findings.evidence: `if (_builtFor == _groups.Count) return;` is the only invalidation. Rows are added at nodes that depend on play (PrivateAt), and systems hold their directory for the simulation's life. No ILoadListener resets them, and GroupTable has no OnRead hook.
findings.failure_scenario: A game saved with N groups continues; private enterprise row N is created at node X and BankSystem's directory is built at N+1. The player reloads, and a different timeline creates row N at node Y. BankSystem's directory still has X→N and no entry for Y. An auction at X with no winning bid assigns the facility to a family based at Y, and if Y is on another continent, PayFromGroup moves coins across continents. An auction at Y creates a duplicate family. The result differs from a run without the reload.
findings.fix: Add a generation counter to GroupTable, bumped in OnRead, and rebuild when it or the count changes.

findings.title: SellBondCommand.Validate mutates state, and offers cached then are used all turn on stale cash
findings.evidence: Validate calls BondDesk.Offered, whose OffersOf writes BondOffers and `offers.Turn = turn`, kept until CreditSystem ends the turn. ICommand says Validate must not mutate anything.
findings.failure_scenario: A SellBondCommand that is then rejected still fixes the week's offers at the start of the turn. Later in the turn InvestmentSystem and CreditSystem raise bonds against those amounts, not the cash after this turn's production and spending, so the NPC bond sales differ from a turn without the rejected command, and a group that has since spent its cash can be taken below zero by `groups.Cash[g] -= part`. Replays stay deterministic because the command is replayed too.
findings.fix: Compute offers without caching when called from Validate, or invalidate the cache at the end of the Commands phase.

findings.title: Paying or charging a nation with no population silently destroys or creates coins
findings.evidence: PayNationHouseholds and PayNationWages do `if (first < 0) return;`, and callers debit first: `_bank.Reserve[n] -= publicWages`, `_bank.Reserve[n] -= drain`, `_purses.Float[nation] -= paid`. The map allows population 0 (Households.cs:50).
findings.failure_scenario: A nation whose nodes all have population 0 in map_nodes.csv pays public wages or suffers a bank run: the reserve falls and nobody receives the coins, so ContinentMoney drops below CoinSupply. FamilyAt's negative charge does nothing there, so a new family's start cash appears from nothing.
findings.fix: Fall back to the nation node's households when no node has people.

findings.title: Loading reassigns owners of bank-held facilities, and can create a funded group from nothing
findings.evidence: GroupSystem.OnLoaded runs AssignOwners on every load, for any row with Group < 0 that is not Owner=Player. PrivateAt adds a group with GroupStartCash without taking the coins from anyone, unlike MoneyLedger.FamilyAt.
findings.failure_scenario: A player with no company has a facility seized (Owner=Bank, Group=-1). Saving and loading during the two-week auction gives it a group, so ComputeHash after the load differs from the save's state. If that node has no private enterprise, for example on an older save, 1,000 coins appear. Close overwrites Group, so the lasting effect in current saves is the hash difference.
findings.fix: Skip OwnerIds.Bank in AssignOwners and charge any newly created group's cash to the households, as FamilyAt does.

findings.title: Goods in a lost warehouse can be stranded: an NPC bankruptcy cancels the claim, and bank seizure never grants one
findings.evidence: GoBankrupt writes `WarehouseClaimUntil[f] = claimUntil`, which is -1 when the facility is no longer the player's, and does not clear the cargo. SeizeFacilities sets no claim, and SeizeStoredCargo leaves what the float could not pay for.
findings.failure_scenario: The player loses a facility with goods in its warehouse, claim 8 weeks. The new operator goes bankrupt in week 6: the claim becomes -1, so MoveCargoCommand is refused and ExpireWarehouseClaims never clears the rows. The goods stay in the save, unreachable, until someone buys the facility back. The same happens after an auctioned facility goes to an NPC.
findings.fix: Keep an unexpired claim in GoBankrupt, and start a claim when a seized player facility is sold to an NPC.

findings.title: MulIntRaw returns 1.4e14 for any value above 2^31 instead of the product, in money paths
findings.evidence: `return (value < 0) != (raw < 0) ? long.MinValue >> FractionBits : long.MaxValue >> FractionBits;` is returned whatever the true product, even for a rate below 1. The managed Fx.MulInt gives the exact answer for the same inputs.
findings.failure_scenario: With the sample figures it is out of reach: a continent's supply stays near 25 million. But a config with InitialCoinSupply in the billions lets one holder pass 2^31. A merchant with 3,000,000,000 coins and an encounter loses 1.4e14 instead of 900,000,000, going deeply negative, and an NPC facility pays a 1.4e14 dividend. Conservation holds, so the audit does not notice. Nothing in config validation stops this.
findings.fix: Compute with a 128-bit product by splitting into high and low parts, or reject configs whose coin scale can reach 2^31.

findings.title: Weekly interest truncates per row, so small debts accrue none
findings.evidence: `_bonds.Interest[r] += rate.MulInt(_bonds.Face[r]) / SimClock.WeeksPerYear;` and the same form for trader loans. The remainder is dropped each week rather than carried.
findings.failure_scenario: A bond row whose face times the yearly rate is below 52 coins accrues 0 forever: at 5% a year, any face under about 1,030. BondDesk.Raise splits each sale over every node and group, so small rows are common, and the rounding always favours the debtor. The issuer pays less than the configured rate in aggregate.
findings.fix: Compute weekly interest as rate.MulInt(Face * elapsed) differences, or carry the remainder per row (a save version bump).

findings.title: MoneyTotals can show stale figures after loading a save with the same turn number
findings.evidence: `if (_computedTurn != world.Get<SimClock>().Turn) Recompute(world);` is the only check, and it has no load listener. FinanceSystem always calls Recompute directly, so results are unaffected; only presentation reads Refresh.
findings.failure_scenario: The UI reads totals at turn 100, then the player loads another save at turn 100. View.NationMoneyTotal shows the previous game's figures until the turn advances.
findings.fix: Reset _computedTurn after a load, through a load listener.

findings.title: Enum arguments of player commands are not validated; a bad guidance axis throws mid-turn
findings.evidence: BuyFacilityCommand and FoundCompanyCommand never check Axis/Focus, while LobbyCommand does check its Policy. GuidanceSystem does `_state.Weights[(int)signal.Axis] += signal.Weight`. SetFacilityControlCommand writes `(byte)Mode` unchecked.
findings.failure_scenario: BuyFacilityCommand(f, price, (GuidanceAxis)99) passes Validate and Apply. In the Guidance phase, after production, markets and finance have run, the index throws. Clock.Advance never runs, so the next AdvanceTurn repeats a turn whose effects are already applied. Reachable only if presentation passes a bad value.
findings.fix: Check the enum range in Validate for these three commands.

findings.title: Buying a facility and founding a company need no presence, even while travelling
findings.evidence: These Validate methods check only ownership and coins. Expansion, cash moves, cargo moves, bonds, loans, licenses and guilds all require standing at the place and not travelling. I found no decision saying remote purchase is intended, and none forbidding it, hence the lower confidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A player mid-voyage with coins of a distant continent buys a facility there at once and marks the node detailed, without travel, toll or encounter risk. A remote bid on an auction works the same way.
findings.fix: If presence is intended, use the PlayerSite check without the ownership part; otherwise record remote purchase as a decision.

strengths: Cross-continent coins: traced PayThere, BuyLoad, SellForCoins, Depart tolls, MerchantFlowJob.Settle and PayWage, BankSystem AcrossContinents, and ExchangeCommand. Each debit and credit balances per continent, and a holder is counted by the same continent rule in ContinentMoney (facility node, merchant home, group node).

Deposits: interest raises PlayerDeposit without coins, but every payout (withdrawal, BuyGoods, road upkeep, seizure, winning bid) is limited by the reserve, so no coins can be conjured from unbacked deposit balance. Loan instalments from deposit net to zero on the reserve.

Credit: bills, bank discounting (BillRoom.SettleBank in the same turn), bond service, player bond purchase and sale at face, price cover (HedgeNet), contracts (the Deliver formula sums to zero), trader loans and migration cash splitting (SendToTowns distributes all of it) all conserve coins.

Determinism: randomness is stateless and keyed by (seed, turn, stream, entity). PriceUpdateJob and ConsumptionJob write only their own market's cells; other jobs are single-threaded in row order. System order has a total tie-break by id. HashSet iteration in PolicySystem only feeds order-independent sums. I found no float or GetHashCode feeding simulation state.
Row removal: every swap-back loop I checked iterates in reverse (orders, contracts, bills, bonds, loans, auctions), and the BondTable and NpcLoanTable indexes follow swaps and reset on read.

Save and load: all AgentTable, FacilityTable, HouseholdCash, CurrencyState and PlayerState migrations produce the layout of their columns in order. Files are parsed and migrated before anything is applied, leftover bytes are refused, rollback restores from a backup, the data hash covers config (GameDatabase.cs:84), and tolls, modifiers, LOD, subsidy rates and production lines are rebuilt on load.
Land bonus cache: ProductionSystem caches output multipliers until the facility count changes. I tried to make it stale, but LandLevel only rises in OpenFacility, which also adds a row, so it holds.

Native memory: every allocation I found in ProductionSystem, PricingSystem, DefenseSystem, ArbitrageMerchantBehavior, MerchantTraitTable and the world tables has a matching DisposeIfCreated on a non-readonly field, safe on double dispose and on a partly built pipeline.
